contracts.title: Exact association of reductions and scans
preconditions: The binary operation is total or fallible over the lane dtype.
The lane is rank one after axis selection.
contracts.success_relation: reduce(f)([x1, ..., xn]) = f(x1, f(x2, ... f(xn-1, xn))); fold_left(f)([x1, ..., xn]) = f(... f(f(x1, x2), x3) ..., xn); scan(f) and scan_left(f) return those values for each nonempty prefix, inclusive.
success_conditions: A singleton lane returns its element unchanged without applying f.
.reassociate() permits another grouping only when failure equivalence is proved, an equivalent algorithm is used, or a separately accepted numeric policy applies.

error_relation.condition: An explicit axis reduction is applied to a rank-zero value.

contracts.mutation_frame: Pure: no input, destination, or host state is modified.
contracts.termination: Total: one application of the binary operation per adjacent pair, so at most n-1 applications for n elements.
contracts.empty_rule: Empty reduce and fold_left lanes use only a registered or explicit identity, else EmptyReduction; empty scans return an empty lane without applying f.
contracts.proof_sketch: Verus: define spec fn right_fold(f, s) by structural recursion on the sequence; prove lemma_reduce_refines_right_fold(s) for the executable reduce, and lemma_singleton_passthrough(x) without any application of f. Kani: a harness over symbolic 3-element I64 lanes with checked subtraction asserts reduce equals the right fold, with cover!() for both a success and an overflow, and a negative control in which a left fold is rejected.

contracts.title: Empty-lane identities and explicit identity
preconditions: The aggregate null policy has already been applied.
An explicit identity, when given, has the output dtype.
contracts.success_relation: For a nonempty lane the result is the exact right reduction of the aggregate operation; for an empty lane it is the registered identity (typed zero for sum, one for product, false for any, true for all) or the explicit .identity(value).
success_conditions: An identity is used for an empty lane only and is never a seed.
Minimum, maximum, and mean have no registered identity.

error_relation.condition: .identity(value) whose dtype differs from the output dtype.

contracts.mutation_frame: Pure: no input, destination, or host state is modified.
contracts.termination: Total: one application of the binary operation per adjacent pair, so at most n-1 applications for n elements.
contracts.empty_rule: This contract is the empty rule for the aggregates it lists.

seeded_mutations.description: Fail an empty sum instead of returning its typed zero.
Combine the explicit identity with nonempty input as an initial seed.

contracts.proof_sketch: Verus: prove lemma_identity_only_on_empty(s, id): s.len() > 0 implies aggregate_with_identity(s, id) == aggregate(s), and s.len() == 0 implies it equals id. Kani: harnesses over symbolic lanes of length 0 to 3 assert the registered identities and that an identity never changes a nonempty result, with cover!() for each length.

contracts.title: Truncating integer division and remainder
contracts.success_relation: idiv(a, b) = trunc(a / b) and rem(a, b) = a - b * idiv(a, b), so the remainder takes the dividend's sign.
contracts.mutation_frame: Pure: no input, destination, or host state is modified.
contracts.empty_rule: Not applicable: binary scalar operation; null operands propagate null.

seeded_mutations.description: Round the quotient towards negative infinity.

contracts.proof_sketch: Verus: prove lemma_idiv_truncates(a, b) relating the executable checked division to the mathematical truncated quotient, and lemma_rem_sign(a, b): rem(a, b) == 0 or sign(rem(a, b)) == sign(a). Kani: an exhaustive symbolic harness over all I64 pairs asserts both relations and the two failures, with cover!() for each sign quadrant.

contracts.title: Explicit dtype conversion
preconditions: The target dtype is Bool, I64, or F64.
contracts.success_relation: Bool to I64 or F64 yields 0 or 1; I64 to F64 rounds to nearest, ties to even; F64 to I64 yields the same integer for finite, integral, in-range values; mixed-dtype arithmetic requires an explicit cast.
success_conditions: Converting to the same dtype returns the value unchanged.

error_relation.condition: F64 to I64 of NaN or an infinity.
F64 to I64 of a non-integral value.
Arithmetic on operands of different dtypes.

contracts.mutation_frame: Pure: no input, destination, or host state is modified.
contracts.empty_rule: Not applicable: scalar conversion; null converts to null.

seeded_mutations.description: Widen mixed I64 and F64 operands silently.

contracts.proof_sketch: Verus: specify cast_f64_to_i64 by the mathematical value of the float and prove lemma_cast_exact(x) for finite integral in-range inputs and lemma_cast_rejects(x) otherwise. Kani: a harness over symbolic f64 bit patterns asserts the error classification for NaN, infinities, 2^63, -2^63, -0.0, and non-integral values, with cover!() for each class.

contracts.title: True division converts operands first
contracts.success_relation: div(a, b) = f64(a) / f64(b), where each operand is first rounded to the nearest F64 (ties to even) and the division is IEEE 754 binary64.
success_conditions: A zero divisor yields a signed infinity or NaN, not an error.
The result can differ from rounding the exact quotient once.
contracts.mutation_frame: Pure: no input, destination, or host state is modified.
contracts.empty_rule: Not applicable: binary scalar operation; null operands propagate null.

seeded_mutations.description: Round the exact rational quotient of I64 operands once.

contracts.proof_sketch: Verus: define div by composing the operand conversion with IEEE division in the specification and prove the executable refines it; no claim about the exact quotient is made. Kani: a harness over symbolic I64 pairs asserts bit equality with (a as f64) / (b as f64), with cover!() for an operand above 2^53.

contracts.title: Validity and three-valued logic
preconditions: Logical operands are Bool or null; no numeric truthiness exists.
contracts.success_relation: and, or, and not follow Kleene three-valued logic; xor is unknown when either operand is unknown; aggregates apply the null policy before reducing: propagate by default, or .skip_nulls() removes invalid values in order.
success_conditions: false and unknown is false; true or unknown is true.
contracts.mutation_frame: Pure: no input, destination, or host state is modified.
contracts.termination: Total: one application of the binary operation per adjacent pair, so at most n-1 applications for n elements.
contracts.empty_rule: .skip_nulls() that removes every value then applies the normal empty rule (SC-02).
contracts.proof_sketch: Verus: model a nullable Bool as Option<bool> and prove the Kleene truth tables and lemma_skip_nulls_then_empty(s). Kani: exhaustive harnesses over the nine operand pairs assert the tables, with cover!() for each unknown result.

contracts.title: F64 special values in binary min and max, sums, and means
contracts.success_relation: Binary min and max follow IEEE 754-2019 minimum and maximum: null takes precedence, then NaN propagates, and -0.0 < +0.0; minimum and maximum aggregate them; an empty F64 sum is +0.0 while a singleton passes through, so sum([-0.0]) is -0.0; mean converts to F64, right-sums, and divides by a count of at most 2^53.
success_conditions: The result of min or max is one of its operands, a NaN, or null.
contracts.mutation_frame: Pure: no input, destination, or host state is modified.
contracts.termination: Total: one application of the binary operation per adjacent pair, so at most n-1 applications for n elements.
contracts.empty_rule: Empty F64 sum is +0.0; empty minimum, maximum, and mean fail per SC-02.

seeded_mutations.description: Return the non-NaN operand of min or max (IEEE minNum and maxNum).

contracts.proof_sketch: Verus: specify ieee_minimum over f64 bit patterns with explicit NaN and signed-zero cases and prove the executable refines it for nullable operands. Kani: a harness over symbolic f64 pairs asserts NaN propagation, the signed-zero ordering, and null precedence, with cover!() for each case, and a negative control in which f64::min (minNum) is rejected.

contracts.title: Cell atomicity
preconditions: A batch has a frame shape and a typed cell schema such as DVec3.
contracts.success_relation: A typed cell is one logical element until an explicit component operation: cardinality is the product of the frame shape, and axes index the frame only.
success_conditions: Batch<DVec3> of shape [2,3] has cardinality 6, not 18.

error_relation.condition: An axis at or beyond the frame rank.

contracts.mutation_frame: Pure: no input, destination, or host state is modified.
contracts.termination: Total: proportional to the frame rank.
contracts.empty_rule: A frame with a zero extent has cardinality zero.

seeded_mutations.description: Expose cell components as an extra axis.

contracts.proof_sketch: Verus: prove lemma_cardinality_excludes_components(frame, cell) and that every valid axis index is below the frame rank. Kani: a harness over symbolic frame shapes of rank up to 3 asserts cardinality and axis rejection, with cover!() for a zero extent.

contracts.title: Atomic output commit
preconditions: An operation writes its result to a destination only at commit.
contracts.success_relation: On success the destination holds the complete output; on failure or cancellation before commit the destination is unchanged.

error_relation.condition: Failure or cancellation before commit, leaving the destination unchanged.

contracts.mutation_frame: Only the destination changes, and only at commit.
contracts.termination: Total: one commit per successful operation.
contracts.empty_rule: An empty output commits an empty destination.

seeded_mutations.description: Write completed elements before the failure.

contracts.proof_sketch: Verus: model the destination as ghost state and prove frame preservation: ensures result.is_err() ==> dest@ == old(dest)@. Kani: a harness injects a failure at a symbolic index and asserts the destination is unchanged, with cover!() for failure at the first and last element.

contracts.title: comb! operator precedence and pipeline staging
preconditions: Source is a token stream accepted by the macro frontend.
contracts.success_relation: The token stream is split on |> first (lowest precedence, left-associative); each stage parses with Rust expression precedence as parsed by syn, restricted to the documented DSL subset in spec/macro-grammar.json.
success_conditions: Comparison mixed unparenthesized with &, |, or ^ is rejected, as are comparison chains.
Closures and || are accepted only inside host { ... }.

error_relation.condition: A rejected construct in spec/macro-grammar.json; the first-screen diagnostic names the rule.

contracts.mutation_frame: Pure: macro expansion has no runtime effects.
contracts.termination: Total: linear in the token count.
contracts.empty_rule: Not applicable: an empty pipeline is a syntax error.

seeded_mutations.description: Group a |> b |> c as a |> (b |> c).

contracts.proof_sketch: No proof: 2.3.1 replays every grammar corpus entry as a trybuild pass or fail fixture, with a completeness check; the recognizer in tools/docs_validation/grammar.py models the corpus, not the macro.
